question: Should OpenClaw core support native cross-gateway session messaging now, and if yes should it use the linked `gateway.peers`/session-tool parameter shape or wait for a broader bridge-protocol design?
rationale: The implementation choice affects gateway trust boundaries, message injection permissions, config/secret surface, and session-state ownership, which automation cannot infer safely from the issue alone.

options.title: Design the federation contract first
options.body: Keep this issue and the linked PR open while maintainers define identity, scopes, transport, replay, and session-history rules, then revise the implementation against that contract.

options.title: Narrow and land the linked PR
options.body: Accept `gateway.peers` as the intended product shape after conflict resolution, security review, upgrade proof, and a real multi-gateway run demonstrating message delivery and history behavior.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Close or redirect the core feature after documenting an external plugin/MCP/bridge approach that does not require missing OpenClaw core APIs.

recommendation.title: Design the federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue and the linked PR open while maintainers define identity, scopes, transport, replay, and session-history rules, then revise the implementation against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history across `sessions_send` semantics and gateway URL/security plumbing, which are the central decision surfaces here.
